h1: Low-FODMAP Macro Calculator for IBS & SIBO
description: Calculate your low-FODMAP macros in seconds: 20% protein, 30% fat, 50% tolerated carbs (Monash protocol). Includes a food list and comparison table. Backed by 70% IBS symptom improvement evidence.

intro: The **low-FODMAP diet** (Monash University, 2005) removes short-chain carbohydrates that ferment in the intestine: **F**ermentable **O**ligosaccharides, **D**isaccharides, **M**onosaccharides **A**nd **P**olyols. It's the most evidence-backed dietary intervention for **irritable bowel syndrome (IBS)** and **SIBO**, improving symptoms in **70% of patients**. The standard macro distribution is **20% protein / 30% fat / 50% carbohydrates**, with carbs sourced exclusively from low-FODMAP foods. The protocol has 3 phases: **1) Elimination (2–6 weeks)**; **2) Gradual reintroduction (6–8 weeks)**; **3) Personalisation**.

example.title: Worked example: 2,000 kcal/day low-FODMAP plan
steps: **Fat (30%)**: `2000 × 0.30 / 9` = **67 g/day** — olive oil, avocado, aged cheese.
**Low-FODMAP carbs (50%)**: `2000 × 0.50 / 4` = **250 g/day** — rice, potato, carrot, quinoa, ripe banana.
example.result: Typical day: chicken breast + rice + carrot + strawberries + olive oil. Avoid onion, garlic, wheat, and lactose-containing dairy.

explanation:
## What is the Low-FODMAP Diet?

Developed at **Monash University (Australia)** in 2005 by Dr. Peter Gibson and Dr. Susan Shepherd, low-FODMAP temporarily removes short-chain carbohydrates that gut bacteria rapidly ferment, producing gas, bloating, cramping, and pain. Clinical trials show **50–80% of IBS patients** report meaningful symptom reduction during the elimination phase. For SIBO (Small Intestinal Bacterial Overgrowth), the diet reduces substrate available to misplaced bacteria, but it does not treat the underlying cause—antibiotic protocols remain the primary SIBO treatment.

> **FODMAP** stands for: **F**ermentable **O**ligo-, **D**i-, **M**onosaccharides **A**nd **P**olyols.

---

## The 5 FODMAP Groups to Restrict

| Group | High-FODMAP Foods | Why It's Problematic |
|-------|-------------------|----------------------|
| **Fructans** | Wheat, onion, garlic, leek | Most common IBS trigger; even small amounts matter |
| **GOS** (galacto-oligosaccharides) | Legumes, broccoli, beetroot | Humans lack the enzyme to digest them |
| **Lactose** | Milk, yogurt, ricotta | Only problematic in lactase deficiency—not everyone needs to cut it |
| **Excess fructose** | Apple, mango, honey, pear | Fructose absorbed poorly when it exceeds glucose in the same food |
| **Polyols** | Cherries, stone fruits, sorbitol (E420), xylitol | Slow, incomplete small-intestine absorption |

**Portion size matters critically.** Many foods are low-FODMAP in small quantities but become high-FODMAP past a threshold—for example, ½ ripe banana is safe, a whole one is not. The official [Monash FODMAP App](https://www.monashfodmap.com/ibs-central/i-have-ibs/get-the-app/) provides tested portion thresholds.

---

## Allowed Low-FODMAP Foods

| Category | Options |
|---------|---------|
| **Grains** | Rice, potato, quinoa, oats (½ cup cooked), polenta, gluten-free pasta |
| **Protein** | Chicken, beef, fish, eggs, firm tofu, canned tuna (in water) |
| **Vegetables** | Tomato, cucumber, carrot, spinach, zucchini, bell pepper, eggplant |
| **Fruit** | Strawberry, ripe banana (½), kiwi, orange, grapes, blueberries |
| **Dairy** | Lactose-free milk/yogurt, aged hard cheeses (cheddar, parmesan, brie) |
| **Fats** | Olive oil, avocado oil, small portion of avocado (⅛ whole fruit) |

Aged cheeses are safe because the fermentation process breaks down lactose to negligible levels.

---

## How This Calculator Works

The calculator estimates your **daily macronutrient targets** within a low-FODMAP food framework using the following distribution:

- **Protein:** 20% of total calories → grams = (kcal × 0.20) ÷ 4
- **Fat:** 30% of total calories → grams = (kcal × 0.30) ÷ 9
- **Carbohydrates:** 50% of total calories → grams = (kcal × 0.50) ÷ 4

These ratios are intentionally moderate—not ketogenic, not very high-carb—because both extremes can complicate FODMAP adherence. Very high-carb diets increase fermentation risk; very low-carb diets often rely on foods (nuts, avocado in large portions, certain vegetables) that can exceed FODMAP thresholds.

### Reference macro table

| Calories | Protein | Fat | Carbs |
|----------|---------|-----|-------|
| 1,500 kcal | 75 g | 50 g | 188 g |
| 1,800 kcal | 90 g | 60 g | 225 g |
| 2,000 kcal | 100 g | 67 g | 250 g |
| 2,200 kcal | 110 g | 73 g | 275 g |
| 2,500 kcal | 125 g | 83 g | 313 g |

---

## The 3 Phases of the Monash Protocol

### Phase 1 – Elimination (2–6 weeks)
Remove all high-FODMAP foods completely. Most patients see significant symptom relief within 1–2 weeks. **Do not extend this phase beyond 6 weeks**—prolonged restriction reduces gut microbiome diversity and is nutritionally incomplete long-term.

### Phase 2 – Reintroduction (6–8 weeks)
Reintroduce one FODMAP group at a time (e.g., fructans in week 1, lactose in week 2), keeping a symptom diary. This identifies *your specific* triggers—most people tolerate 3–4 of the 5 groups without symptoms.

### Phase 3 – Personalization (lifelong)
Resume a varied diet, avoiding only the specific groups confirmed as triggers. This phase is nutritionally sustainable and protects long-term microbiome health.

---

## What This Calculator Does NOT Include

- **Fiber targets** – adequate fiber (25–38 g/day) is important but must come from low-FODMAP sources (oats, carrots, rice bran). This requires separate tracking.
- **Micronutrient gaps** – eliminating legumes, wheat, and many fruits temporarily reduces calcium, iron, B vitamins, and folate. Consult a registered dietitian for supplementation guidance during Phase 1.
- **Calorie needs assessment** – enter your own estimated TDEE; the calculator does not calculate it from height/weight/activity.
- **Medical diagnosis** – IBS and SIBO require clinical diagnosis. This tool supports dietary management, not treatment.

---

## Common Mistakes

1. **Using "gluten-free" as a synonym for "low-FODMAP."** Gluten-free products can contain high-FODMAP ingredients like apple juice concentrate, honey, or inulin.
2. **Ignoring cumulative load ("stacking").** Eating several low-FODMAP foods in the same meal can collectively exceed safe thresholds.
3. **Skipping Phase 2.** Staying in permanent elimination denies you the microbiome diversity your gut needs and makes the diet unnecessarily restrictive.
4. **Assuming garlic-infused oil is high-FODMAP.** Fructans are water-soluble, not fat-soluble—garlic-infused oil contains negligible FODMAPs and is safe.

---

*Always implement the low-FODMAP diet under guidance of a registered dietitian with GI specialization, particularly if you have a confirmed SIBO diagnosis or concurrent conditions such as Crohn's disease or celiac.*

faq.q: What is the standard low-FODMAP macro split?
faq.a: The Monash University protocol uses **20% protein, 30% fat, and 50% carbohydrates** as the starting distribution. The key constraint is that carbs must come from low-FODMAP sources — not from wheat, onion, garlic, legumes, or high-fructose foods.

faq.q: How many grams of carbs on low-FODMAP for 2,000 kcal?
faq.a: At 2,000 kcal with 50% carbs: `2000 × 0.50 / 4` = **250 g of carbohydrates per day**, from tolerated sources like rice, potato, quinoa, oats (½ cup cooked), ripe banana, strawberries, and carrots.

faq.q: How long does the elimination phase last?
faq.a: **2 to 6 weeks**, depending on symptom severity. It's not recommended to extend beyond 6–8 weeks because prolonged elimination can reduce gut microbiota diversity.

faq.q: Does the low-FODMAP diet cure IBS or SIBO?
faq.a: It doesn't cure either condition, but improves symptoms in **70% of IBS patients** (2017 meta-analysis). For SIBO, it works best when combined with antibiotic or herbal antimicrobial treatment prescribed by your doctor.

faq.q: Can vegetarians or vegans follow low-FODMAP?
faq.a: It's challenging but possible. Most plant proteins (legumes, seitan) are high-FODMAP. Tolerated options: **firm tofu** (not silken), **tempeh** (small portions), canned and rinsed chickpeas or lentils (max ¼ cup). A dietitian familiar with low-FODMAP is essential.

faq.q: What is Phase 2 and why does it matter?
faq.a: Phase 2 is the **reintroduction phase** (6–8 weeks). You test one FODMAP group at a time: 3 test days with increasing portions, then 3 washout days before testing the next group. This identifies *which* specific groups trigger your symptoms — most people are sensitive to only 1–2 groups, not all.

faq.q: What's the best app for checking FODMAP foods?
faq.a: The **Monash FODMAP app** (official, iOS and Android) is the gold standard — 1,000+ foods with red/yellow/green ratings by serving size. Also useful: FODMAP Friendly app.

faq.q: Is low-FODMAP a permanent eating plan?
faq.a: No. Elimination is temporary (2–6 weeks). After completing Phase 2 reintroduction, Phase 3 personalises your diet — most people avoid only the 1–3 groups that trigger their specific symptoms and eat freely otherwise.
